boilerMetallurgies.name: Traditional Leaded Machining Brass (CW614N / CuZn39Pb3, ~1.5–3.0% Pb)
boilerMetallurgies.description: Standard free-machining brass containing microscopic insoluble lead globules dispersed at the grain boundaries to facilitate high-speed lathe turning. When exposed to hot organic acids during descaling, the lead and zinc phase selectively dissolve (dezincification), creating a porous, lead-enriched surface layer that sheds massive amounts of toxic lead (up to 800–1,200 µg/L) during initial post-descaling shots.

boilerMetallurgies.name: Surface-Treated / TEA-Coated Low-Lead Brass (NSF/ANSI 372 Compliant)
boilerMetallurgies.description: Brass treated via chemical plating (TEA - Ternary Eco Alloy, tin-nickel-phosphorus alloy) or Ruveco selective acid-depletion process. The chemical process depletes surface lead atoms down to a depth of 50 µm, creating an impervious passive barrier that restricts lead leaching below 0.25% weighted surface standards, provided harsh abrasive descalers do not mechanically strip the micro-coating.

boilerMetallurgies.name: Die-Cast Aluminum Thermoblock with Embedded Stainless Tube
boilerMetallurgies.description: Cast aluminum alloy block containing an embedded internal coiled stainless steel or copper fluid conduit. High thermal conductivity allows sub-60-second warmup. However, aluminum is amphoteric; exposure to strong acidic descalers (sulfamic acid) or alkaline cleaning tablets strips the native aluminum oxide film, causing severe pitting, white aluminum hydroxide flaking, and galvanic corrosion at the copper-aluminum interface.

boilerMetallurgies.name: Dual AISI 316L Surgical Stainless Steel Boilers
boilerMetallurgies.description: Heavy-gauge austenitic stainless steel alloyed with 16–18% chromium, 10–14% nickel, and 2–3% molybdenum. Highly impervious to pitting corrosion from chlorides and organic descaling acids. Exhibits virtually zero lead or copper leaching under high pressure and temperature (95°C at 9 bar), representing the ultimate hygienic gold standard in espresso extraction engineering.

descalingRegimes.name: Hot Citric Acid Solution (50 g/L • 90°C • pH 2.1)
descalingRegimes.description: Conducting citric acid descaling at full brew temperature (90°C) is a major hazard for leaded brass. Citrate ions aggressively chelate dissolved Cu2+ and Pb2+ ions, shifting the thermodynamic equilibrium to accelerate metal dissolution. Hot acid strips the protective cuprous oxide (Cu2O) patina, triggering severe toxic leaching spikes documented in BfR espresso machine studies.

descalingRegimes.name: Sulfamic Acid Commercial Descaler (30 g/L • 60°C • pH 1.5)
descalingRegimes.description: Inorganic amidosulfonic acid (H3NSO3) used in commercial espresso service. Dissolves calcium carbonate scale up to 10x faster than citric acid without generating insoluble calcium citrate precipitates. However, its low pH (1.5) requires strict exposure timing (<20 minutes) and comprehensive multi-reservoir neutral flushes to prevent aggressive attack on brass fittings and silicone boiler gaskets.

descalingRegimes.name: Ambient-Temperature Citric Acid (30 g/L • 25°C • pH 2.4)
descalingRegimes.description: Descaling solution pumped through the hydraulic circuit while the machine is completely cold (20°C–25°C). The absence of thermal acceleration suppresses galvanic dissolution and prevents excessive dealloying of brass boiler components while still dissolving loose limescale deposits.

descalingRegimes.name: Distilled White Vinegar / 5% Acetic Acid (50 g/L • 85°C • pH 2.4)
descalingRegimes.description: A destructive domestic descaling myth. Acetic acid dissolves copper and lead to form copper acetate (verdigris) and toxic lead acetate ('sugar of lead'). It permeates porous EPDM and silicone grouphead gaskets, leaving lingering sour off-flavors that persist for dozens of brew cycles and accelerating dezincification of brass fittings.

descalingRegimes.name: Baseline SCA Brewing Water (150 ppm TDS • 93°C • pH 7.2)
descalingRegimes.description: Optimally remineralized brewing water (calcium hardness 50–70 ppm CaCO3, alkalinity 40–50 ppm, zero chlorides). Maintains a stable, micro-thin protective mineral passivation layer on internal boiler walls, keeping metal migration well within WHO and EPA drinking water limits.

hydrodynamicScenarios.name: Vibratory Solenoid Pump (9.0 Bar • 250 mL/min • 0.7mm Gicleur)
hydrodynamicScenarios.description: Standard home espresso pump operating at 50/60 Hz pulses. Delivers oscillating pressure peaks that exert mechanical shear on internal boiler scale and corroded oxide crusts, dislodging microscopic metal-rich particulate into the extraction water stream.

hydrodynamicScenarios.name: Commercial Rotary Vane Pump (9.2 Bar • 450 mL/min • Constant Hydrodynamic Flow)
hydrodynamicScenarios.description: Direct-drive commercial rotary pump delivering smooth, pulse-free laminar water flow at high volume. Continuous fluid circulation prevents stagnant concentration boundary layers but accelerates mass transfer of dissolved ions from boiler walls.

hydrodynamicScenarios.name: Stagnant Overnight Boiler Dwell (12h Inactive Reservoir at 20°C → 93°C Warmup)
hydrodynamicScenarios.description: Water sits motionless inside the hot water boiler and heat exchanger for 8 to 12 hours overnight. Without flow dilution, dissolved lead, copper, and zinc ions diffuse steadily from unpassivated brass into the standing water, causing the notorious 'first-morning espresso cup' contamination spike.

hydrodynamicScenarios.name: Steam Boiler Thermal Flash Purge (1.4 Bar Saturated Steam • 126°C)
hydrodynamicScenarios.description: Purging hot water or steam from the service boiler. Because steam venting expels pure H2O vapor, dissolved non-volatile minerals and leached heavy metals continuously concentrate inside the residual liquid boiler water over days of operation.

flushingProtocols.name: Zero Post-Descaling Flush (Immediate Extraction of First Shot)
flushingProtocols.description: Catastrophic user error. The user brews espresso immediately following descaling without running clean water flushes. The shot contains concentrated acid solution and high levels of stripped metal ions (Pb > 1,000 µg/L, Cu > 5,000 µg/L).

flushingProtocols.name: Single Water Reservoir Flush (1.5 Liters Total Throughput)
flushingProtocols.description: Running one full reservoir of clean water through the grouphead. While sensory sourness is reduced, dead legs in the heat exchanger and solenoid valve conduits still retain elevated colloidal lead and copper exceeding EPA action thresholds.

flushingProtocols.name: Certified NSF Multi-Reservoir Purge (3 Full Tanks • 4.5+ Liters Through Group & Steam)
flushingProtocols.description: Gold standard engineering protocol. Purges 1.5L through the grouphead, 1.5L through the hot water tap, and 1.5L through the steam wand. Completely removes residual descaling acids, re-establishes a neutral pH (7.0–7.4), and allows re-passivation of brass surfaces.

flushingProtocols.name: Sodium Bicarbonate Neutralizing Buffer Flush (10 g/L NaHCO3 + 3L Clean Water)
flushingProtocols.description: Flushing a mild sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) buffer solution through the circuit to immediately neutralize residual hydronium ions (H+), halting ongoing acid dealloying and precipitating soluble lead/copper into insoluble carbonates before the final clear water purge.
